Ezra Holt.narrative: I am a quarrier, and a good one; I can read a seam of stone the way other men read weather. Last year I led the crew up the ridge and we cut into stones that were not stones, and I swear by the Hearth I did not know what they were until the giants came down. Now the shelf is closed and Josiah Crane presses me to answer for it, and I will not climb that ridge again for any master's order. I owe Tavvik for meat and I pay when I can, and I do not sleep well when the wind comes off the mountains.
values: an honest day's work for an honest wage
goals: keep my place with Josiah Crane without climbing the ridge
pay off what I owe Tavvik before he comes asking
find stone enough to fill the Lanternquay order from somewhere else
hear no more talk of the cairn
learn to dress a block himself, so he is not only the man who finds the stone
take Bramwell out to the low faces on a quiet day and show him what honest stone looks like

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She says I was careless and she is not wrong, and I would rather she did not say it at the table.

relations.name: Bramwell Holt
relations.label: son
relations.note: He carries water up to the crew and hears too much of the men's talk.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He pays well and presses hard; he wants ridge stone and I will not get it for him.

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: foreman
relations.note: He worked the cutting beside me and has not gone back up either; we do not speak of it.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: A giant who carries meat down the track; I owe him and I dread the day he collects.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: accuser
relations.note: Hollbrenna's son wants me to answer for the cairn, and I have no answer that would satisfy him.

relations.name: Ambrose Vell
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: He rents my crew a kiln yard and has not turned us out over the cairn, which is more than some would.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A builder who thinks quarrymen are paid too much and work too slow.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: the elder
relations.note: She forbade the shelf to all of us for what my crew cut into, and I cannot blame her, and I cannot undo it either.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She carries stone down the fish road and asks after the ridge; I tell her what I can and no more.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: friend's wife
relations.note: She begs Silas to take the fish road instead of the stone road, and I cannot say she is wrong to.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He owes me nothing and I owe him for a load of props; he has been robbed twice and still loads the cart, and I want that road kept open.

memories.gist: The morning we broke into the cairn: flat dressed stones in a ring, and then the giant standing on the ridge above us, saying nothing.
Hollbrenna's word coming down the track: the shelf closed to Kettlebridge, and no quarry crew to climb the ridge.
Josiah Crane in the quarry yard, asking how much ridge stone the Lanternquay order still needs, and not liking my answer.
Tavvik setting down a haunch of meat at the yard gate and saying he would be paid, slowly if need be.
Bramwell carrying the water up and standing too close while the men talked of the cairn.
Corin dressing a block in the yard, and telling me plain that I should have known better.

stances.why: I have said it a hundred times and it is true; no quarrier cuts a cairn on purpose.
Whatever Josiah offers, the giants are up there and I am not going to meet them.
A debt to a giant is not one to let sit; he has been patient and I would keep him so.
They have families on the terrace and I led them up the ridge once already.
Corin will say her piece and Bramwell is listening; better the yard hears it than the house.

Ezra Holt.secret: I have walked up the track alone at dusk to look at the broken cairn and left a flat stone on it, and I have told no one, not even Corin.
pastimes: sitting by the works fire with a mug, listening to the crews argue about nothing
walking the low meadows at dusk, reading the ground underfoot out of habit
playing at dice with Silas Vance and losing more often than he likes
Ezra Holt.calling: I read stone the way other men read weather, and I want to go on reading it with my crew beside me and no ridge above us.

Corin Holt.narrative: I am a mason, and I dress the stone my husband's crew raises; a block that is not square is a block that will not hold. I keep the quarry tally for Josiah Crane and I know to the load how much ridge stone the Lanternquay order still wants, and that is the trouble: Ezra will not climb and I cannot make him. He was careless up there and I tell him so at home, because someone must. I fear the giants will come down the track one day, and I keep the yard swept and the tally straight so that whatever comes, our house is in order.
goals: get the Lanternquay order filled from some other face
make Ezra face what he did without breaking him
keep Bramwell away from the ridge and the talk of it
keep Josiah Crane satisfied with the tally
be given a face of her own to work, not only the tally and the yard
teach Bramwell to set a level true, so he has a trade in his hands whatever his father does

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good quarrier and a stubborn man; he was careless on the ridge and he will not hear it twice.

relations.name: Bramwell Holt
relations.label: son
relations.note: He listens at the yard gate and comes home with the men's talk in his head.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He wants his stone and he is right to want it; I keep the tally so he cannot say we cheated him.

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: foreman
relations.note: He was beside Ezra at the cutting and he will not speak of it either; two men keeping one silence.

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She said plainly the cutting was wrong, and I respect her for it though it is my husband she speaks of.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: master's daughter
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books and asks after the tally; she is fair and she does not nag.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: giant
relations.note: He brings meat down the track against the elder's word, and one day that will bring the elder down too.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: A giant of the shelf I have never met, and I would rather it stayed that way.

relations.name: Corwin Vance
relations.label: foreman's son
relations.note: He works the quarry floor and thinks his father has gone soft about the ridge; I have heard him say the cairn was only stones, and I do not care for it.

memories.gist: The day the crew came down off the ridge with their tools on their shoulders and would not say what they had found.
Josiah Crane reading the tally aloud in the yard and asking where the ridge stone was.
Dressing a block in the yard while Ezra sat on the wall and would not look at the ridge.
Bramwell asking me what a cairn is, and me not knowing what to tell him.
Odile Vance saying at the well that the cutting was wrong and the giants had right on their side.

stances.why: If the masters cannot trust the count they will not trust the crew, and we live by the crew.
I will not pretend at my own table that he did right; someone in this house must say it.
They are patient, not forgiving, and the track runs to our town.
He is eleven and afraid of it already; he does not need the men's talk to make it worse.
The Lanternquay order must be met and there is stone in the lower faces that no giant ever laid.

Corin Holt.secret: I have twice written the ridge loads in the tally as though they came from the lower face, because Josiah would not take 'none' for an answer.
pastimes: dressing a block in the yard when the tally is done, just to keep her hand in
walking to the clock tower square on market day to hear what the other masons say of their work
keeping a small herb plot by the door and trading cuttings with Odile Vance
Corin Holt.calling: A block that is not square is a block that will not hold, and I would be a mason of dressed stone until my hands give out.

Bramwell Holt.narrative: I carry the water up to the crew in a bucket that is too big for me, and I like the quarry because there is always something happening. Since the cairn was cut the men go quiet when I come near, and my father does not go up the ridge any more. My mother says I am not to go up there either, and I do not want to: I saw the giant on the skyline once and I still dream of it.
values: keeping out of the men's way
goals: carry the water without spilling it
be allowed to hold the measuring rod
not to go up the ridge
carry the water up the whole way without spilling a drop
be let to hold the measuring rod for a real cut
Bramwell Holt.mood: watchful, a little frightened, eager to be useful

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is the best quarrier in Kettlebridge and he does not go up the ridge any more.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She dresses the stone and keeps the tally, and she says the ridge is not for me.

relations.name: Silas Vance
relations.label: foreman
relations.note: He was at the cutting and he has not gone back up either; he is kind to me in the yard.

relations.name: Perry Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He climbs the clock tower steps and I climb the quarry spoil; we race.

relations.name: Nella Marsh
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She knows her letters and reads the crate marks to me.

memories.gist: Seeing a giant standing on the ridge above the quarry, still as a stone, while the men below said nothing.
Carrying the water up and the men stopping their talk when I came near.
My mother asking me what a cairn is and me not being able to answer.

stances.why: My mother said not to, and the giant is up there.
If I carry the water well they let me stay and listen.

pastimes: carrying the water bucket up to the crew and being told he is useful
playing at quoits and tag with Perry Fenwick and Nella Marsh
watching the masons dress stone and copying the ring of the chisel on a scrap
Bramwell Holt.calling: I want to hold the measuring rod and be one of the crew, and one day read the stone like my father.
